page: Microsoft Azure EC20ads_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. The instance features 20 dedicated vCPUs derived from 10 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor operating on the x86_64 architecture. Hardware-level cache provisioning includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. Cryptographic and bit manipulation acceleration is available via AES, VAES, SHA_NI, BMI2, ADX, and AVX instructions, though AVX-512 extensions are not supported on this configuration.

System memory is configured at 160.0 GB of RAM, establishing a high 8 GB per vCPU ratio suitable for memory-bound computational tasks. Local scratch storage consists of an integrated 805 GB solid-state drive (SSD), which eliminates the need to route temporary input and output traffic through attached network disks. This configuration lacks dedicated hardware GPU acceleration, focusing entirely on general CPU compute and memory capacity.

Benchmark results for the EC20ads_v5 register consistently across the middle tier for its resource class. The AMD EPYC processor achieved a single-core score of 1991.24 and a multi-core score of 22267.27 in stress-ng evaluations. In Geekbench testing, it recorded 1273.0 points for single-core throughput and 9346.0 points across all cores, reaching 16207.0 points in Clang compilation and 19727.0 points in ray tracing tasks. PassMark evaluation yielded a CPU score of 21155.77 and a memory score of 2178.49. In data management testing, the instance delivered 7297.06 points in PassMark database operations and achieved 16.85 million operations per second during Redis SET benchmarking.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the bundled 805 GB SSD provides built-in local capacity for intermediate files, reducing secondary storage expenditures for high-throughput I/O pipelines. The 8:1 memory-to-core balance presents efficient hardware density for workloads that require substantial RAM allocations without necessitating oversized CPU counts. Tradeoffs include the absence of AVX-512 support and an unaccelerated graphics pipeline. The instance fits in-memory caching solutions like Redis, relational database hosting, software build systems, and medium-scale enterprise analytics.
